title: What If You Could See How Many Days Everyone Has Left?

shots.vo: On his seventeenth birthday, Kai woke up and saw a number above everyone's head.

shots.label: BIRTHDAY, 7:00 AM
shots.vo: It started with a headache. A sharp one. Right behind his eyes.
Happy birthday, sweetheart! Seventeen! How does it feel?
Floating above his mom's head was a number. Fourteen thousand eight hundred ninety two.
Mom... is there something above your head?
Just my hair, honey. Breakfast in five.

shots.label: WALKING TO SCHOOL
shots.vo: Outside, it was everywhere. Every single person had a number.
The old man at the bus stop had nine hundred. The baby in the stroller had thirty thousand.
Old people have small numbers. Babies have big ones. These are days. Days until they die.
He could see exactly how much time everyone had left.

shots.label: SCHOOL
shots.vo: At school, he tried not to look up. It didn't work.
Yo, birthday boy! Why are you staring at my forehead?
Jace. The most annoying guy in school. His number said three.
Three? Three days?
Kai! Happy birthday! I got you something!
Mia. His best friend since they were six. The girl he'd never told how he felt.
Then he looked up.
Earth to Kai? Why do you look like you've seen a ghost?
Above Mia's head was the smallest number he had seen all day.
His best friend had three days left to live.
Kai can see how many days everyone has left. His best friend Mia has three.

shots.label: DAY 1
shots.vo: Kai didn't hear a single word in class. He just watched Mia.
Three days. What happens in three days? A car? A disease? Some freak accident?
Okay, you're being weird. Like, weirder than usual.
Can I walk you home today? And tomorrow? And... the day after that?

shots.label: AFTER SCHOOL
shots.vo: He walked between her and the street. He checked every corner twice.
Are you my bodyguard now? Should I pay you?
Then Mia stepped off the curb. And a bus came around the corner.
Mia! No!
He yanked her back. The bus missed her by an inch.
Okay. Okay. You just saved my life. How did you know?
Kai looked up. He'd saved her. The number should have changed.
It hadn't. It still said three.

shots.label: THAT NIGHT
shots.vo: That night, he couldn't sleep. If the bus wasn't it, then what was?
Okay. If I can see everyone's number... what's mine?
He walked to the mirror. He had never been this scared of his own reflection.
Above his own head, the number glowed red.
Three. The same as Mia.
Whatever was coming in three days... it was coming for both of them.
Kai and Mia both have three days left. And Kai is the only one who knows.

shots.label: DAY 2
shots.vo: Mia, I need to tell you something. And you're going to think I'm crazy.
He told her everything. The headache. The numbers. The bus.
So we're both going to die tomorrow. Cool. Very romantic birthday story, Kai.
I can prove it. Pick anyone. I'll tell you their number.
Fine. Her. The girl with the dog.
Zero. Her number is zero. Mia, she's going to die today.
They watched her, terrified. And then a guy ran up and got down on one knee.
She said yes. The whole park clapped.
Her number hit zero. And she didn't die. She got engaged.
So... your death numbers are actually proposal numbers?

shots.label: GRANDPA'S HOUSE
shots.vo: Kai needed answers. And there was one person who always had them.
You turned seventeen. Headache behind the eyes. Numbers everywhere. Am I right?
Grandpa... you can see them too?
Every man in our family. Since my grandfather. Sit down, kid.
Those numbers aren't death, Kai. They're the days until your life changes forever.
But listen to me. Sometimes the change is the best day of your life. And sometimes it's the worst.
So how do I know which one it is?
You don't. My number hit zero twice. Once when I met your grandmother. Once when I lost her.
Kai and Mia had two days left. Best day of their lives. Or the worst.
The numbers aren't death. They count down to the day your life changes forever.

shots.label: DAY 2, AFTERNOON
shots.vo: Kai had a new theory. Him and Mia. Same day. Same change.
What if it's us? What if the big change is... us?
Then he saw Jace. Walking with Mia. His number also said two.
No. No no no. Not Jace. Anyone but Jace.

shots.label: LUNCH
shots.vo: So Kai did something stupid. He sat down right between them.
Fun fact, Mia. Jace still sleeps with a night light. Shaped like a duck.
Bro, what is wrong with you? I was asking her about a school project.
Kai. Seriously. You're embarrassing yourself.
She grabbed her tray and left. She didn't look back.
Dude. Just tell her you like her. Everybody knows. Except her.

shots.label: THAT EVENING
shots.vo: Kai went to Mia's house to apologize. And to finally tell her.
But Mia was already crying when she opened the door.
Mia, I'm sorry about lunch. I was an idiot. I just—
It's not about lunch, Kai. My dad got a job. In Canada.
We're moving. In two days.
Two days. That was the change. Mia was leaving forever.
And Kai had forty eight hours to stop it. Or to finally tell her the truth.
Mia is moving to Canada in two days. Kai has one plan. It's a terrible plan.

shots.label: 11 PM
shots.vo: Step one. No moving truck, no move.
At midnight, Kai snuck over to Mia's driveway with a bag of potatoes.
One potato in the exhaust pipe. Works in every movie.
Then the porch light turned on.
Kai. Why are you holding a potato?
This? This is... a goodbye potato. It's a tradition.
Mia laughed so hard she cried. For a second, everything felt normal.
But Kai saw it. The number above her head had changed. One.

shots.label: DAY 3
shots.vo: The next morning, Kai walked into school. And froze.
Every single student. Every teacher. Every number said one.
This isn't about Mia moving. Something is going to happen to the whole town.

shots.label: GRANDPA'S HOUSE
shots.vo: Grandpa! Everyone in town has the same number! What does that mean?
Grandpa went quiet. Then he took out an old newspaper.
Nineteen eighty seven. The whole town hit zero. That was the night of the great storm.
But the weather says sunny all week.
It said sunny in nineteen eighty seven too.
One day left. A storm nobody saw coming. And only Kai knew.
The whole town has one day left. A storm is coming. Nobody believes it.

shots.label: DAY 3, 9 AM
shots.vo: Kai stood up in the middle of history class.
Everybody listen! A huge storm is hitting the town tonight. We need to get ready!
Silence. Then the whole class burst out laughing.
Bro checked the weather app and chose violence.

shots.label: PRINCIPAL'S OFFICE
shots.vo: Ten minutes later, Kai was in the principal's office. Suspended for causing panic.

shots.label: NOON
shots.vo: So he went door to door. He warned neighbors. Shop owners. Strangers.
Most of them shut the door in his face. Some called his mom.
Kai! I heard you got suspended for yelling about a storm?
Mia. Everyone has a one. Everyone. Something terrible happens tonight. Please believe me.
Mia looked at him for a long time. Then she took out her phone.
My cousin works at the weather station. I'm asking her.
Three minutes later, her phone buzzed.

messages.text: a system just formed off the coast
if it turns it hits us TONIGHT

shots.vo: Okay. I believe you. What do we do?

shots.label: 4 PM
shots.vo: They made a plan. The school gym had no windows and a basement. It was the safest place in town.
So you're actually serious about this storm thing?
Then you need way more people. My team has a group chat with two thousand members.
Then the lights flickered. Outside, the sky turned green.
Every number in town dropped to zero. The storm was here.
Every number just hit zero. The storm nobody believed in is here.

shots.label: THE STORM
shots.vo: Wind tore through the streets. Trash cans flew like paper.
Everyone to the school gym! Go! Go!
Thanks to Jace's group chat, hundreds of people made it inside.
Kai! Oh thank god. I'm so sorry I didn't believe you.
Grandpa was there. Jace's family. Half the school. But someone was missing.
Where's Mia? She was right behind me!
He called her. Once. Twice. Then a text came through.
Theo. Mia's little brother. Eight years old. Alone in the storm.
Kai, don't you dare go out there!
But he was already gone.
The rain hit like needles. A street sign spun past his head.
Kai! Wait up! You're not doing this alone!
Jace? Why?
Because you were right and I laughed at you. Now move!

shots.label: MIA'S HOUSE
shots.vo: Mia's front door was ripped off its hinges.
Kai! Down here! Mia's stuck!
Mia was pinned under a fallen bookshelf. And she wasn't moving.
Grandpa's words echoed in his head. Sometimes it's the best day of your life. And sometimes the worst.
Mia is trapped under a bookshelf in the middle of the storm. And she isn't moving.
Jace! Grab that side! On three!
They lifted with everything they had. The shelf moved an inch. Then two.
Theo pulled his sister free.
She came back for me. She wouldn't leave without me.
Mia. Mia, please. Open your eyes.
Nothing. Then she coughed.
Did you... bring a potato?
Kai laughed and cried at the same time.
You came back for me. You idiot. You actually came back.
I'll always come back for you. Always.
Then the roof groaned. The whole house was about to give.
We have to go. Now!
Jace carried Theo. Kai carried Mia. They ran into the storm.
They could see the gym. Two hundred meters. One hundred.
Kai! They're closing the gym doors because of the wind!
Then run faster!
Then a huge branch tore off a tree. Right above Kai.
He had one second. He pushed Mia forward.
In the last second, Kai saw his own reflection in a car window.
His number said zero.
And then everything went black.
Kai saved Mia from the storm. Then everything went black.

shots.label: THREE DAYS LATER
shots.vo: Beep. Beep. Beep. Kai opened his eyes.
He's awake! Doctor! He's awake!
Mom? Where's Mia? Is she okay? Is Theo okay?
Everyone's okay, sweetheart. Because of you. Nobody in town got seriously hurt.
On the TV, the news was playing his story.

banner.text: TEEN WHO PREDICTED THE STORM SAVED HUNDREDS

shots.vo: Kai looked up at his mom. And something was wrong.
There was no number above her head. Nothing.
He looked at the doctor. The nurse. The people in the hallway. Nothing. Nothing. Nothing.
They're gone. The numbers are gone.
Mom... is there something above my head?
Just your hair, honey. And it really needs a wash.

shots.label: LATER
shots.vo: Of course they are. Your number hit zero. Your life changed. That's how it works.
So I'll never see them again?
Not everyone's. When I met your grandmother, I stopped seeing everyone's number. Except one.
Hers?
Hers. For forty years. Every morning.
Then there was a knock on the door.
Hey, hero. I brought you something.
Kai looked up at her. And for the first time in three days, he saw a number.
Only one. Above Mia. And it wasn't a number he expected.
The numbers are gone. Kai can only see one now. Mia's.
The number above her head was glowing pink. Twenty three thousand.
Why are you staring at my forehead again? Do I have something on my face?
No. It's just... are you still moving to Canada?
Dad turned the job down. He said this town needs everyone right now. So... I'm staying.
Mia. I have to tell you something. I should have told you years ago.
That you like me? Kai, you were holding a potato at midnight. Everyone knows.
For the record... I like you too. Since we were six.

shots.label: ONE MONTH LATER
shots.vo: One month later, the town was rebuilt. Kai and Mia were inseparable.
Yo, lovebirds! Theo wants a rematch at basketball!

shots.label: GRANDPA'S HOUSE
shots.vo: Grandpa. Her number is twenty three thousand. What happens then?
Twenty three thousand days. That's about sixty years. Your grandmother's number was the same, once.
So that's... the rest of her life?
No, kid. That's how long you two get together. Go check your own.

shots.label: THAT NIGHT
shots.vo: That night, Kai stood in front of the mirror again. Not scared this time.
There it was. Glowing pink. Twenty three thousand. The exact same number.
Some numbers count down to the worst day of your life. Some count down to forever.
If you could see your number... would you look?
